title: Maintain an explicit public API
requirement: Stable functions and domain models must be exported deliberately from lss4py; experimental modules must not be presented as stable. Pre-1.0 breaking changes must update documentation and tests in the same change.
verification: Import tests and review of the README stable API list against the intended top-level stable exports.

title: Accept backend-neutral observed data
requirement: Public tabular analytical APIs must accept the governed eager dataframe input protocol rather than require callers to use Polars; row and case identity must use explicit keys or positions rather than a pandas index contract.
current_gap: Stable private kernels use Narwhals and typed results, and event-log lead time has explicit keys and pandas/Polars parity. Shared parity coverage for every public calculation is incomplete; PyArrow remains provisional.
verification: Run the same contract fixtures with pandas and Polars inputs, plus provisional PyArrow cases, non-default pandas indexes, explicit keys, and unsupported/lazy input errors.

title: Keep the process-model contract explicit
requirement: Process-aware calculations must consume normalized ProcessModelIR. Per-call arguments override IR bindings. Automatic .flo parsing is not part of the core analytical contract unless a later ADR changes that boundary.
verification: Binding-precedence, missing-binding, and IR construction tests.

title: Make event-log topology semantics deterministic
requirement: Event-log-aware APIs must use explicit case, step, start, and end bindings. Parallel and rework behavior must be declared in the process model; ambiguous overlap or repetition must fail validation.
verification: Sequence, parallel, rework, unknown-step, overlap, and repeat tests.

title: Reject invalid analytical inputs explicitly
requirement: The stable current-Yellow-Belt public analytical APIs must validate required bindings and columns, time ordering, denominators, binary stage domains, and declared event-log topology as applicable. Domain failures must use an appropriate LSS4PyError subtype rather than silently coercing an invalid result.
verification: Negative-duration, denominator, binary-domain, missing-binding, overlap, repeat, unknown-step, and event-log warning tests for the stable public slice.

title: Treat percentiles as first-class outputs
requirement: Duration summaries and comparisons must provide p50, p90, p95, p99, and count through a reusable result model. The quantile method, interpolation, key handling, and missing-data policy must be documented and tested.
current_gap: No governed duration-summary API exists.
verification: Deterministic fixtures covering odd/even and small samples, missing data, skew, ties, backend parity, and key attribution.

title: Validate R SixSigma parity with versioned fixtures
requirement: Each claimed compatibility feature must include inputs, expected outputs generated with R SixSigma 0.11.1, numerical tolerances, invalid-input cases, provenance, and intentional semantic differences. Plot pixel parity is not required.
current_gap: No cross-language fixtures are currently checked in.
verification: Automated Python tests against checked-in fixture data and provenance metadata; compatibility status changes only after tests pass.

title: Separate calculation from rendering
requirement: Statistical calculations must return usable data without rendering. Plotting and document production consume result objects and remain optional dependencies.
verification: Base install/import and stable-slice analysis tests run without visualization or document-rendering extras.

title: Use typed analytical result models
requirement: Every multi-value public analysis must return a versioned typed model containing estimates, units, limits where relevant, assumptions, warnings, method metadata, and interpretation context. Plain dictionaries and upstream library results are not stable study contracts.
current_gap: Timing and yield result models exist; map_process returns a TypedDict and planned studies are not implemented.
verification: Static type checking, construction/serialization tests, and public result contract snapshots.

title: Preserve the analytics-core dependency boundary
requirement: lss4py may depend on foundational analytical and compatibility libraries, but must not depend on deliverables or labs packages. Polars is the governed canonical ingestion engine; other concrete dataframe, simulation, optimization, process-mining, visualization, and storage engines must be isolated or optional.
current_gap: pandas is optional, Polars is the governed ingestion dependency, private kernels are isolated, and the duplicate analytics layer is removed. Optional-extra matrix coverage remains incomplete.
verification: Dependency metadata inspection, import-boundary checks, base installation smoke tests, and optional-extra matrix tests.
evidence: pyproject.toml; lint_imports_config.ini; ADR-0002; ADR-0004; ADR-0018; ADR-0019

title: Run repository quality gates
requirement: Changes to supported code must pass lockfile validation, the locked test suite, Ruff, and ty.
verification: Run uv lock --check, uv run --locked pytest, uv run --locked ruff check ., and uv run --locked ty check.
evidence: All repository gates passed on 2026-10-07; 46 tests passed, 5 planned behaviors remained xfailed, coverage was 93.04%, and all 6 import-linter contracts were kept.

title: Keep examples reproducible and auditable
requirement: Governed examples must declare input data and provenance, run from the locked environment, avoid hidden state, and state analytical assumptions, chosen method, and expected outputs.
current_gap: The README quick start exists. Governed worked examples and parity fixtures remain part of the v0.3 Yellow Belt MVP.
verification: Execute examples in a clean environment and compare key results with checked-in expectations.

title: Normalize adapter outputs at the core boundary
requirement: File, database, and telemetry adapters must translate source data into documented tabular or event-log contracts before invoking calculations. Source SDKs and credentials must not leak into analytical APIs.
current_gap: CSV interval-event logs normalize to a typed IntervalEventLog backed by the canonical Polars schema and feed per-case lead time. General tabular, database, telemetry, OCEL, and XES adapters remain unimplemented.
verification: Contract tests run identical calculations against equivalent in-memory and adapter-loaded inputs plus schema, timestamp, key, and source-failure cases.
evidence: src/lss4py/adapters/event_log.py; src/lss4py/domain/interval_event_log.py; src/lss4py/_event_log.py; tests/test_event_log_ingestion.py; ADR-0018; ADR-0019

title: Use Narwhals as the analytical dataframe compatibility boundary
requirement: Eager native frames must enter public tabular analytical APIs through Narwhals IntoFrame/from_native handling. Narwhals is a runtime dependency; core file adapters materialize Polars under ADR-0018, while pandas remains an optional compatibility backend.
current_gap: Stable timing and yield kernels use Narwhals and CSV ingestion materializes Polars inside IntervalEventLog. Complete pandas/Polars contract coverage remains incomplete; PyArrow is provisional.
verification: Dependency and type checks plus contract tests for pandas, Polars, and provisional PyArrow analytical inputs; no pandas-specific index contract in public results.
evidence: https://narwhals-dev.github.io/narwhals/; ADR-0004; ADR-0009; ADR-0018; ADR-0019; src/lss4py/_kernels

title: Make materialization and copy behavior explicit
requirement: The initial analytical API must accept eager inputs only and reject lazy/distributed frames with an actionable error. Core file adapters materialize Polars; conversion into Polars or numeric arrays must define null conversion, ordering, dtype, copy, and materialization behavior.
current_gap: CSV interval-event ingestion documents Polars materialization, preserves source row order, and exposes explicit copy behavior through IntervalEventLog.to_polars(). Broader lazy-input, dtype, and null-policy coverage remains incomplete.
verification: Lazy-frame rejection tests, dtype/null/order fixtures across backends, and tests that document permitted copies and materialization boundaries.

title: Return backend-neutral keyed metric results
requirement: Per-row or per-case calculations must return an LSS4PY keyed metric result with explicit keys or positions, numeric values, unit, name, and metadata; conversion helpers may produce a requested native frame without changing the canonical result.
current_gap: Per-case event-log lead time returns a keyed TimingResult independent of the input backend. Native-frame result conversion helpers and complete duplicate/non-string key coverage remain incomplete.
verification: Round-trip tests to pandas and Polars, duplicate/non-string key tests, serialization tests, and value/key ordering parity.

title: Enforce cross-backend analytical equivalence
requirement: Every public tabular calculation must run a shared backend contract suite. Supported backends must produce numerically equivalent governed results, errors, ordering, null handling, and identifiers within documented tolerances.
current_gap: Per-case event-log lead time has pandas/Polars equivalence coverage. The shared suite does not yet cover every public tabular calculation; PyArrow remains provisional.
verification: Parameterized pandas/Polars test suite and provisional PyArrow fixtures; every backend-specific exception requires documentation and a regression test.

title: Delegate numerical primitives behind governed kernels
requirement: General statistical primitives should use NumPy, SciPy, statsmodels, or another reviewed dependency behind small LSS4PY kernel interfaces. Direct implementations require a documented formula, authoritative reference, and focused numerical tests.
current_gap: The private _kernels boundary is implemented and import-enforced. Numerical reference coverage is incomplete for the broader roadmap.
verification: Architecture/import tests, upstream comparison tests, extreme/boundary numerical fixtures, and ADR review for new direct algorithms.
evidence: ADR-0003; ADR-0016; ADR-0019; lint_imports_config.ini; src/lss4py/_kernels; pyproject.toml

title: Provide an analysis suitability registry
requirement: Analysis methods must declare their supported questions, required fields, outcome/predictor types, sampling/design prerequisites, assumptions, alternatives, and interpretation limits in machine-readable metadata.
current_gap: Eight supported calculations have immutable decorator-registered metadata and deterministic candidate queries. Dataset suitability checks and metadata for future study workflows remain incomplete.
verification: Registry completeness tests, deterministic question-to-candidate fixtures, and tests that guidance never executes a method without an explicit selection.

title: Record analysis provenance and interpretation context
requirement: Every governed result must record method/version, parameters, input schema or fingerprint, cohort/window definition, missing-data policy, backend, library versions, assumptions, warnings, and creation time as applicable.
current_gap: Stable timing and yield results include a provenance envelope, assumptions, and interpretation context. Cohort, missing-data, library-version, and rerun coverage remain incomplete.
verification: Serialization snapshots, rerun/reconstruction tests, version metadata checks, and omission tests for required provenance fields.

title: Model CTQs and specifications explicitly
requirement: A validated analytical specification model must represent CTQ name, unit, direction, target, LSL/USL, defect/opportunity definition, grouping, time window, and declared decision context without conflating specification and control limits.
current_gap: The declaration model is implemented and validated. Automatic filtering, defect classification, and direct specification arguments to analytical methods are separate future analytical integration work.
verification: tests/test_specification.py covers one/two-sided and targetless specifications, units, opportunities, invalid limits, immutable copies, windows, versioned serialization, and explicit describe reuse.

title: Implement reusable data-quality and distribution diagnostics
requirement: A backend-neutral diagnostic layer must compute schema, missingness, uniqueness, duplicates, descriptive statistics, governed percentiles, skew/tail indicators, and supported distribution/normality diagnostics without mutating input.
current_gap: No governed diagnostic or descriptive-summary API exists.
verification: Known-distribution, skew, multimodal, missing, duplicate, backend-parity, small-sample, and warning-threshold fixtures.

title: Implement yield and capability kernels
requirement: Governed kernels must calculate defect/rework Yield, FTY, RTY, DPMO and normal capability Cp/Cpk/component indices/Z using explicit denominators, specification models, variation estimates, and supported confidence intervals.
current_gap: Only binary funnel-stage yield exists; no capability calculation is implemented.
verification: R parity, textbook, one/two-sided, degenerate-variation, missing, confidence-interval, and property-based formula tests.

title: Implement an extensible SPC engine
requirement: SPC calculations must separate chart family, baseline/Phase I estimation, Phase II application, limit formulas, sample-size handling, rule evaluation, signal provenance, and rendering. Moving range is the first required family.
current_gap: No governed SPC calculation is implemented.
verification: R moving-range parity, published constant/formula fixtures, phase/baseline tests, variable sample-size tests, rule tests, and chart-family contract tests.

title: Implement governed measurement-system analyses
requirement: Measurement-system kernels must validate crossed/nested/attribute/stability study designs and return ANOVA or agreement results, variance components, repeatability/reproducibility, study variation, tolerance contribution, distinct categories, uncertainty, and diagnostics as applicable.
current_gap: No MSA implementation exists.
verification: R ss.rr parity, AIAG-style reference fixtures where licensing permits, balanced/unbalanced/invalid design tests, and broader MSA method fixtures.

title: Implement quality-loss kernels
requirement: Quality-loss calculations must support scalar/vectorized nominal-, smaller-, and larger-the-better conventions and aggregate coefficient, MSD, average loss, and optional production loss in typed results.
current_gap: No quality-loss implementation exists.
verification: R ss.lf/ss.lfa parity, closed-form examples, zero/infinite target conventions, unit/cost validation, and vector/scalar equivalence tests.

title: Implement profile-monitoring workflows
requirement: Profile analysis must separate profile normalization/smoothing, Phase I prototype and bands, Phase II outside-band proportions and labels, tolerance evaluation, and plotting.
current_gap: No profile analysis exists.
verification: R profile-function parity fixtures, smoothing parameter tests, profile orientation/key tests, threshold boundaries, and calculation-without-plot tests.

title: Implement inferential comparison kernels
requirement: Inference APIs must separate estimand, design, assumptions, estimator, confidence interval, hypothesis test, effect size, multiplicity context, diagnostics, and interpretation. Supported methods must include governed common mean, paired, proportion, and nonparametric comparisons.
current_gap: No confidence-interval or inferential comparison engine exists.
verification: Published examples, SciPy/statsmodels comparisons, edge/sample-size tests, effect/interval/test consistency, and misuse-warning fixtures.

title: Implement regression and designed-experiment kernels
requirement: Modeling APIs must preserve formula/design metadata, randomization/blocking, main effects/interactions, coefficient uncertainty, residual diagnostics, collinearity/influence information, validation data, and prediction-vs-causal interpretation.
current_gap: No regression or DOE workflow exists.
verification: statsmodels comparison fixtures, known factorial designs, rank-deficiency and alias tests, residual/validation checks, and serialization snapshots.
evidence: ADR-0003; R package DOE example-data scope

title: Implement process-discovery and conformance contracts
requirement: Observed process discovery, bottleneck/variant analysis, and declared-model conformance must use separate result types, preserve case/step evidence, and isolate optional PM4Py integration behind adapters.
current_gap: map_process provides only nodes and transition counts; bottleneck and conformance analyses are absent.
verification: Trace fixtures with loops/parallelism/variants, PM4Py adapter contract tests, ranking evidence tests, and declared-vs-discovered type separation.

title: Implement reproducible decision-support engines
requirement: Queueing, Monte Carlo, discrete-event simulation, and optimization workflows must record inputs, seeds, assumptions, objectives, constraints, solver/status, scenarios, distributions, and robustness/sensitivity results.
current_gap: Simulation is a placeholder; optional dependencies exist without governed workflows.
verification: Seed reproducibility, analytical benchmark, infeasible/unstable optimization, queueing-consistency, scenario, and optional-dependency isolation tests.

title: Define visualization contracts over result models
requirement: Analytical plots must consume typed results or explicit governed data, return library-native plot objects, preserve units/limits/signals, avoid hidden recalculation, and remain optional.
current_gap: No stable visualization layer exists.
verification: Plot smoke/semantic tests, calculation independence tests, label/unit/limit assertions, and no-visualization base-install checks.

title: Define a versioned neutral analysis-bundle schema
requirement: A serialization contract must package typed results, provenance, assumptions, warnings, specifications, and input references in a backend-neutral versioned format suitable for notebooks and downstream deliverables.
current_gap: AnalysisBundle exists but is experimental and too small for governed provenance.
verification: Schema round trips, compatibility/migration tests, unknown-version failure, pandas/Polars-free load, and golden bundle fixtures.

title: Implement non-normal capability methods cautiously
requirement: Capability analysis must support explicitly selected transformations, fitted non-normal distributions, or empirical approaches with fit diagnostics, tail-extrapolation warnings, method provenance, and sensitivity comparison.
current_gap: No non-normal capability behavior exists.
verification: Known non-normal simulations, transformation round trips, fitted-distribution comparisons, tail-sensitivity fixtures, and insufficient-fit warnings.

title: Implement categorical quality analyses
requirement: Categorical analysis must preserve counts and denominators and support Pareto summaries, proportions, contingency tests, effect estimates, expected-count diagnostics, and optional plots.
current_gap: No categorical quality-analysis API exists.
verification: Known count tables, sparse/zero cells, unequal denominators, exact/asymptotic method selection, Pareto stability, and backend-parity tests.

title: Version control plans and signal rules
requirement: A control-plan model must version metric/specification references, baseline data or fingerprint, limits, sampling cadence, rule set, ownership metadata, signals, acknowledgements, and recalibration events; limits must never move implicitly.
current_gap: No control-plan or persistent signal model exists.
verification: Serialization/versioning, immutable-baseline, rule replay, acknowledgement, recalibration-audit, and drift/SPC integration tests.

title: Govern reference datasets and fixtures
requirement: Reference datasets must include stable identifiers, version, provenance, license/redistribution status, schema, intended analyses, checksums, and expected results or citations. Test fixtures and teaching datasets must be distinguishable.
current_gap: No governed dataset catalog exists.
verification: Manifest validation, checksum, license/provenance completeness, schema load, expected-result regression, and redistribution policy checks.

title: Distribute wheel and verify PyPI packaging
requirement: Each stable release must produce valid wheel and source distributions using uv build, pass PyPI metadata validation, support verified installation, and verify import success from the published package.
current_gap: No explicit distribution verification is part of current release process.
verification: Build with uv build returning exit 0, twine check for metadata compliance, test PyPI upload dry-run, clean environment pip install from PyPI, and import smoke tests.
